title: Evaluate arithmetic expressions
prompt: Implement evaluate(expr) in expr.js. It evaluates an arithmetic expression over decimal numbers (`42`, `3.5`) with + - * / % and ^ (power), unary minus and parentheses, ignoring whitespace. Precedence from low to high: + and -; * / and %; unary minus; ^. All binary operators are left-associative except ^, which is right-associative, and the right operand of ^ may itself start with a unary minus. So -2^2 is -4 and 2^3^2 is 512. Division or remainder by zero throws a RangeError. Anything malformed throws a SyntaxError whose message contains `at N`, where N is the 0-based index in the input of the offending character (the input's length when it ends too early). Do not change test.js.
